project: L-H Battery Company Plant (Jeffersonville, Ohio)

notes: Scope later grown to a $2.8B re-announcement with ~200 permanent jobs (status_source, 2025-01-14) - not summed into promised_capital_usd per re-announcement discipline. 20-year SAF offtake agreement with Southwest Airlines (up to 680M gallons). Status source states construction expected to take ~2 years after engineering concludes, followed by a 6-8 month commissioning period, but gives no calendar year for first output.

project: Our Next Energy ONE Circle Gigafactory (Van Buren Township)
current_status: PRODUCING (pilot LFP cells); pivoted from EV to defense/rail/grid after losing largest EV customer, ~45% staff cut, ~60% of building vacant
notes: 20 GWh capacity, full capacity promised by end of 2027; ~$215-237M state incentives (MEDC disbursed $70M of up to $237M, then paused). Pilot LFP cell production started Nov 2023, ahead of promised 2024. Jan 2026: lost largest EV customer, suspended EV battery investment, retooled for defense/rail/grid storage cells.

project: Röhm Bay City MMA Plant
current_status: AT VOLUME
notes: First C2-based MMA plant in North America, 250,000 t/yr, using Röhm's LiMA technology; Röhm owned by Advent International, OQ Chemicals supplies feedstock. Groundbreaking Oct 27, 2022. Officially opened / reached worldwide-first full industrial scale June 2026; ~90 employees reported at status. Promised completion shifted: announcement targeted mechanical completion 2023, groundbreaking release said completion early 2024.

project: Rivian Normal Plant R2 Expansion
current_status: PRODUCING; R2 ramping with accelerated hiring
notes: Expansion of Rivian's existing Normal, IL EV assembly plant to add R2 SUV production, raising total site capacity to 215,000 units/yr; R2 run rate targeted at up to 155,000 units/yr when fully scaled.

project: ENTEK Lithium Separators Terre Haute
current_status: UNDER CONSTRUCTION; DOE disbursed first $77.2M of up-to-$1.3B loan (Sept 2025)
notes: Lithium-ion battery separator plant, Vigo County Industrial Park II, Terre Haute. DOE (Sept 17, 2025) announced disbursement of $77,217,590 against an up-to-$1.3B DOE loan; DOE cites ~763 construction jobs and 635 operations jobs upon completion.

project: Octapharma Critical-Care Manufacturing Facility, Rock Hill
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; final approvals secured, production expected mid-2030s
notes: Octapharma's first U.S. manufacturing facility, a plasma-derived critical-care/biologics production campus at Palmetto Research Park (former Carolina Panthers HQ site), ~50-acre site in Rock Hill, York County. Press release states groundbreaking and construction timeline to be released later.

project: Diamond Green Diesel Port Arthur
current_status: PRODUCING; ~470M gal/yr renewable diesel, SAF upgrade underway (expected Q1 2025)
notes: 50/50 JV of Darling Ingredients and Valero Energy, adjacent to Valero's Port Arthur refinery. Capacity ~470 million gal/yr renewable diesel. Began operations late 2022, ahead of the announced second-half-2023 target. A $315M SAF upgrade (converting ~50% of capacity to sustainable aviation fuel) was expected to complete Q1 2025 per Jan 2024 reporting. No promised_jobs figure stated in the sources.

project: Natron Energy Sodium-Ion Battery Gigafactory (Kingsboro Megasite, Edgecombe County)
current_status: CANCELLED; Natron ceased all operations Sept 3, 2025 before construction; facility never built
notes: Nearly 1.2 million sq. ft. facility at the 437-acre Kingsboro megasite; planned 24 GWh annual sodium-ion battery capacity. Governor's release cites 1,062 JDIG-tied jobs and $3.4B economic growth over 12 years. Natron closed its Michigan and California facilities (~95 layoffs) after failing to raise funding; no NC incentive payments were made since targets were never met.

project: Southern Energy Renewables Green Methanol and SAF Facility (St. Charles Parish)
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; construction planned late 2027, commercial operations targeted late 2029; no ground broken
notes: Greenfield plant converting regional wood-waste biomass into green methanol and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). First commercial-scale U.S. facility for Southern Energy Renewables. LED cites 120 direct new jobs (avg salary $97,267) and 514 total/regional job opportunities; 514 is a regional figure, not direct. Project positioned ahead of a proposed merger with DevvStream.

project: AbbVie Durham Manufacturing Campus
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; construction slated to begin 2026, no groundbreaking reported
notes: 185-acre campus near Research Triangle Park; first-phase small-volume parenteral (SVP) sterile-injectable drug-product manufacturing plus next-gen labs and warehouse, serving immunology, neuroscience and oncology medicines. Described as AbbVie's largest-ever single-campus capital investment; U.S. center of excellence for SVP manufacturing.

project: Toyota Indiana BEV SUV (Princeton)
current_status: PRE-PRODUCTION; Princeton BEV SUV line not yet in production
notes: $1.4B is the initial April 25, 2024 announcement for the Princeton (Toyota Indiana) facility; the release also cites $8B cumulative total investment in Toyota Indiana and $18.6B across all US operations since 2021 (cumulative context, not this project). Adds a battery-pack assembly line using lithium-ion cells from Toyota Battery Manufacturing North Carolina. Distinct from Toyota's separate $1.3B Kentucky BEV SUV project.

project: Microporous Lithium-Ion Battery Separator Plant (Southern Virginia Megasite)
current_status: UNDER CONSTRUCTION; groundbreaking May 22, 2026; completion targeted Q3 2027; not yet producing
notes: Two-phase build on Lot 1 of the Southern Virginia Megasite (Berry Hill), Danville/Pittsylvania County. Original 2024-11 announcement: $1.35B and 2,015 direct jobs. Later cited $1.6B investment and 'more than 1,800' jobs at the May 2026 groundbreaking are re-announcements per rule 4; original anchor figures used. Distinct site/company from the ENTEK separator plant.

project: Albemarle Lithium Mega-Flex Facility (Richburg, SC)
current_status: PAUSED; groundbreaking deferred (Mar 2024) amid lithium-price collapse; no restart confirmed
notes: ~$1.3B battery-grade lithium hydroxide 'Mega-Flex' processing plant near Richburg, Chester County, SC; ~50,000 t/yr initially, expandable to 100,000 t/yr. Promise source states construction expected to begin late in 2024 (not a first-output date). Mar 18, 2024 status: Albemarle told investors it would hold off building the facility as lithium prices tanked from 2022 highs; groundbreaking deferred. No credible source confirms a restart since.

project: Cleveland-Cliffs Middletown Works green-steel DRI project
current_status: CANCELLED; hydrogen/DRI green-steel plan abandoned. Per late-Feb 2026 Ohio EPA air-permit filing Cliffs now plans to refurbish the existing coal blast furnace and add a waste-gas cogeneration plant.
notes: Middletown Works, Middletown OH. Original plan: replace coal blast furnace with hydrogen-ready flex-fuel DRI plant plus two electric melting furnaces (near-zero-emissions green steel). DOE grant of up to $575M total (Middletown share cited as ~$500M) via the $6.3B Industrial Demonstrations Program (IRA-funded). Promise source states no explicit production/first-output date; only construction 'primarily starting in 2025 and expected to conclude by 2029'. As of Mar 2026 reporting the DOE grant reportedly remains intact but its revised use is unresolved; Cliffs now intends to start construction on its 'Energy Recovery and Advanced Efficient Ironmaking Project' on Sept. 29, 2026.

project: Toyota TMMK Georgetown BEV (three-row Highlander EV)
current_status: DELAYED; production not started, now targeted January 2027 at the earliest (initially H2 2026)
notes: $1.3B builds on a prior May 2023 $591M announcement per the KY release; the initial production timing (H2 2026) is stated by the status source, as the Feb 2024 promise release gave no production date.

project: Braidy Industries Aluminum Rolling Mill (Unity Aluminum), Greenup County KY
current_status: CANCELLED; never built — missed financing deadlines, renamed Unity Aluminum, project relocated out of KY; state recouped $15M and ~205-acre site donated back by Sept 2022
notes: Capital later cited ~$1.6B; original announcement figure ($1.3B) used per re-announcement discipline. ~1,000 construction jobs excluded from promised_jobs (direct only = 550). Company renamed Unity Aluminum; Steel Dynamics partnered and relocated the aluminum-mill project out of Kentucky. Kentucky recouped its $15M seed investment by Sept 2022 and ~205 acres plus a spec building were donated back to the Northeast Kentucky Regional Industrial Authority. Mill never produced anything, as construction never commenced.

project: Smithfield Foods Sioux Falls Processing Facility
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; in city permitting/TIF and regulatory approvals; site work targeted spring 2026, groundbreaking H1 2027, production by end of 2028
notes: Greenfield combined packaged-meats and fresh-pork facility (up to $1.3B, ~1.1M sq ft on a 211-acre Foundation Park site) that would replace the century-old Sioux Falls plant. Highly automated. Timeline contingent on infrastructure, permitting, construction conditions and final board design approval.

project: Hanwha Pine Bluff Arsenal Energetic Materials Plant
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; enhanced-use lease awarded, no groundbreaking yet
notes: U.S. Army awarded Hanwha Defense USA an enhanced-use lease covering approximately 1,065 acres at Pine Bluff Arsenal to build a ~$1.3B facility producing energetic materials (components used in explosives and propellants) for munitions. Agreement is preliminary, pending final negotiations and due diligence. Distinct from Hanwha's Philly Shipyard. Neither source states a promised or actual first-output date.

project: L3Harris Virginia Advanced Propulsion Facilities (VAPF), Orange County
current_status: ANNOUNCED; design/planning phase, not yet under construction
notes: Solid rocket motor production expansion (VAPF) more than doubling the existing 256,000 sq ft of manufacturing space (mixing, grinding, casting and final assembly) for DoD programs. Builds on a smaller ~$41M April 2024 modernization at the same site. Capital cited as ~$1.265B in the L3Harris release and rounded to $1.3B by Manufacturing Dive.

project: Wanhua Chemical MDI Complex (Convent, St. James Parish)
current_status: CANCELLED; Wanhua dropped its St. James Parish land-use application, project off
notes: Site selection/confirmation announced Nov 2018 ($1.25B, 170 direct jobs, 1,000 construction jobs, MDI for polyurethane, Convent). Project dropped per WWLTV Sep 9, 2019 amid cost escalation (St. James Parish President cited the price tag ballooning from $1.25B to more than $2B), U.S. steel/aluminum tariffs, and community/environmental opposition (RISE St. James); the later >$2B figure is a cost increase, not a re-announced expansion. Wanhua stated it would change the project scope and was reviewing a new location; still committed to a smaller U.S. plant elsewhere. Complex never built.

project: Shintech Plaquemine PVC/VCM Expansion
current_status: PRODUCING (expansion completed 2024)
notes: $1.3B package covered Plaquemine (Iberville Parish, ~$1.25B) plus Addis (West Baton Rouge Parish); the Plaquemine portion is this row. Distinct from Shintech's separate ~$3.4B Plaquemine chlor-alkali/ethylene/VCM expansion announced March 2026 (targeted for completion by end of 2030).

project: MP Materials 10X Northlake
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; site selected, engineering and equipment acquisition underway, commissioning targeted 2028
notes: Greenfield 120-acre NdFeB rare-earth permanent-magnet manufacturing campus in Northlake, Denton County, TX; distinct from MP's existing Fort Worth 'Independence' magnet plant (<10 miles away). Capital 'more than $1.25 billion'; 'more than 1,500 direct manufacturing and engineering jobs'.

project: American Battery Factory Tucson Gigafactory
current_status: PRE-PRODUCTION; offtake secured and financing being finalized; production slated late 2027
notes: ~$1.2B capital investment, ~2M sq ft LFP battery cell gigafactory on Pima County Aerospace Research Campus. Broke ground Oct 26, 2023. Announcement promised initial factory module built within 18-24 months and first-phase construction completed by 2025; per March 2026 status, ABF secured 4.5+ GWh binding offtake and production is now slated for late 2027.

project: Eastman Molecular Recycling Facility Longview
current_status: ON HOLD; under review after DOE revoked $375M grant (May 2025)
notes: Second U.S. molecular recycling (methanolysis) facility, ~110,000 metric tonnes/yr of hard-to-recycle plastic; over 200 full-time jobs plus ~1,000 temporary construction jobs. DOE revoked a $375M grant in May 2025; Eastman reassessing scope, timing and location. Capital figure ($1.2B) stated in status_source.

project: KORE Power KOREPlex Battery Cell Gigafactory (Buckeye, AZ)
current_status: CANCELLED; site listed for sale, DOE $850M loan never closed
notes: 214-acre Buckeye site purchased April 6, 2022; construction started 2022. Capital cited as $1.2B (incl. $850M federal loan) in promise_source and $1.25B in status_source. Cancelled/shelved as of Feb 6, 2025: founder/CEO Lindsay Gorrill stepped down (Jay Bellows hired as new CEO), a general contractor filed a ~$10.4M lien, and the conditional $850M DOE loan never materialized.

project: Martinez Renewable Fuels
current_status: PRODUCING renewable diesel; operating amid USW Local 5 strike-turned-lockout and understaffing (2026)
notes: Conversion of the idled 113-year-old Martinez, CA refinery to renewable diesel; full nameplate ~730 million gallons/year targeted with build to full capacity in 2023. First processing-unit startup Nov 19, 2023 caused a fatality-injury fire. Company laid off 700 workers in 2020 and had ~220 when it resumed operations as a renewable fuel refinery in 2023. Capital figure ~$1.2bn per promised_date_source (nsenergybusiness); the promise_source press release states no dollar figure or job count.

project: USA Rare Earth Blacksburg magnet and metal plant
current_status: UNDER CONSTRUCTION; broke ground Sep 9, 2026
notes: 800,000 sq ft on a 124-acre site in Bailey Industrial Park, Cherokee County; producing sintered NdFeB permanent magnets and strip-cast metal/alloy. Status source (groundbreaking release) states commissioning targeted to begin in 2028; the announcement release states operations online in April 2028.

project: Montana Renewables MaxSAF Expansion (Great Falls)
current_status: PRODUCING; expansion ramping (~60M gal/yr SAF now, target ~200M gal/yr by end 2028)
notes: Expansion of Montana Renewables' Great Falls refinery, which has operated since late 2022 (~140M gal/yr biofuels; ~60M gal/yr SAF currently). Financing is a $1.67B DOE loan facility ($1.44B principal + $233M capitalized interest); conditional commitment Oct 16 2024, closed Jan 10 2025; Phase 1 $782M funded Feb 2025. Original MaxSAF expansion estimated ~$1.2B toward ~315M gal/yr; revised (Sep 2026) to ~$137M remaining capital, with the final DOE Phase 2 draw cut to $34M (from ~$658M) by repurposing adjacent Calumet asphalt-plant equipment. Ramp targets: >80M gal/yr end 2026, >120M spring 2027, ~200M gal/yr end 2028.

project: Encina Point Township Circular Manufacturing Facility
current_status: CANCELLED; Encina withdrew the proposed project in April 2024 and it will not be built
notes: Advanced/chemical recycling (pyrolysis) plant to convert post-consumer plastics into BTX aromatic feedstock. Project proposed April 2022, never built. Inside Climate News (Apr 26 2024): 'A Giant Plastics Chemical Recycling Plant Planned for Pennsylvania Died After Two Years.' Encina said it was reviewing new, bigger locations overseas.

project: Amgen Holly Springs Second Drug Substance Facility
current_status: UNDER CONSTRUCTION; broke ground Jan 24, 2025
notes: Second drug-substance (biologics) plant at the existing Holly Springs campus; this $1B investment brings total planned regional investment to ~$1.5B including a prior $550M 2022 commitment (not summed per re-announcement rule). Carolina Journal cites 'more than 700 jobs to Wake County by 2030' as a combined/regional figure; the 370 here is the direct new-jobs figure from Amgen's release.

project: BMW Plant Spartanburg EV Expansion
current_status: NOT YET PRODUCING; investment complete, iX5 assembly scheduled before end of 2026
notes: $1.7B total US investment announced 2022-10-19 = $1B to prepare Plant Spartanburg for EV production + a separate $700M high-voltage battery assembly plant in Woodruff, SC (a different site, 300 jobs, not summed here per one-site-one-project). Announcement stated at least six fully electric BMW X models by 2030; the iX5 will be the first fully electric BMW assembled in the US, per the 2026 status release the $1.7B investment is complete.

project: Graphic Packaging International Waco CRB Mill
current_status: PRODUCING; first saleable rolls Oct 2025, ramping to full production in 12-18 months
notes: Greenfield coated recycled paperboard (CRB) mill on a 119-acre campus in Texas Central Park, Waco (McLennan County); 640,000 sq ft, 500,000 tons/yr capacity, ~230 direct jobs at ~$65,000 avg salary. Began operating ahead of schedule. East Angus, Quebec plant to close Dec 23, 2025 once Waco is operational.

project: Enel 3Sun USA Solar Gigafactory (Tulsa Port of Inola)
current_status: ON HOLD; work stalled spring 2024, proceeds only if a US investor takes majority stake (as of late 2024)
notes: 3 GW/yr bifacial heterojunction (HJT) cells and modules in a 2M+ sq ft plant, scalable to 6 GW with ~900 more phase-two jobs. ~1,800 construction jobs cited separately (excluded from promised_jobs). Enel CEO Cattaneo said the project advances only with a majority US investor; no 2025-2026 update located.

project: Ascend Elements Apex 1 Hopkinsville
current_status: CANCELLED; Chapter 11 bankruptcy (spring 2026), ~50% built, never operational; sold at bankruptcy auction to Turner-Kokosing JV for $31.7M (June 2026)
notes: $310M Phase 1 within an announced up-to-$1B multi-phase investment; ~400 direct jobs; groundbreaking anticipated Q4 2022. Makes lithium-ion battery cathode active material (pCAM) via Hydro-to-Cathode recycling. Filed Chapter 11 in spring 2026; facility ~50% complete and never operational; sold at bankruptcy auction to a Turner-Kokosing joint venture for $31.7M in early June 2026; new owners seeking a buyer to finish it.

project: Leprino Foods Lubbock Plant
current_status: PRODUCING; first phase ramping (~300 employees by March 2025, ~600 by 2026)
notes: Greenfield 850,000-sq-ft mozzarella cheese and dairy-nutrition plant on 258 acres in East Lubbock; described by Lubbock EDA as the city's largest-ever private investment. Groundbreaking summer 2022 (site groundbreaking image dated 2022-06-16). Second phase slated to bring total employment to ~600 by 2026.

project: Boeing South Carolina 787 Final Assembly Expansion (North Charleston)
current_status: UNDER CONSTRUCTION (broke ground 2025-11-07)
notes: New ~1.2M-sq-ft final assembly building near Charleston International Airport to raise 787 output to a rate of 10 airplanes per month in 2026. Groundbreaking held 2025-11-07; site/staging work underway as of Aug 2025.

project: Mercedes-Benz EV Production Vance/Tuscaloosa (EQ SUV)
current_status: PRODUCING; builds EQS SUV, EQE SUV and Maybach EQS SUV, battery packs from Bibb County plant
notes: $1B initial 2017 announcement (EV production at Vance/Tuscaloosa assembly plant plus a new lithium-ion battery plant in Bibb County, more than 600 new jobs). Cumulative ~$6.8B total once all expansions complete is later re-announcement per rule 4, not summed. Bibb County battery plant is operational and supplies packs to the assembly line.

project: Monolith Materials Olive Creek 2 (OC2), Hallam NE
current_status: NOT STARTED; construction not yet begun as of ~March 2026, company plans to begin construction later in 2026
notes: Methane-pyrolysis plant making carbon black and low-carbon ammonia. Promise source states 'hundreds of good-paying advanced manufacturing jobs' with no specific number, so promised_jobs left empty. Original conditional ~$1B DOE Title XVII loan guarantee lost (status source: 'halted last year when Monolith lost more than $900M in loan guarantees from the US Department of Energy'); project since rescoped to four production units (~220,000 t/yr carbon black, largest US carbon black plant) and shifting feedstock from natural gas to heavy residual fuel oil.

project: Lyten Lithium-Sulfur Gigafactory (Reno AirLogistics Park, Stead)
current_status: CANCELLED (Jan 2026); lease with Reno-Tahoe Airport Authority not agreed; Lyten pivoted to acquiring ex-Northvolt plants in Europe. Never broke ground or produced.
notes: Announced >$1B, 1.25M sq ft, up to 10 GWh/yr, initially 200 jobs growing to more than 1,000. Cancelled January 2026.

project: DENSO Manufacturing Tennessee (DMTN) Maryville electrification expansion
current_status: PRODUCING; plant operating and manufacturing inverters for hybrid vehicles and electrification components
notes: Expansion of DENSO's existing Maryville plant (DMTN, established 1988) to add electrification (EV inverter) and advanced-safety production, making it a North American hub. Lead reports ~4,500 employees across DENSO's Tennessee sites as of 2025.

project: Waaree Solar Americas Brookshire
current_status: PRODUCING; expanding capacity
notes: Initial nameplate promised 3 GW/yr; commercial production commenced January 2025 at 1.6 GW. April 2025 the company announced doubling Texas capacity to 3.2 GW; further expansion targets 5 GW by 2027 and an integrated solar cell facility. 546,000 sq ft in Brookshire, TX (outside Houston).

project: Analog Devices Beaverton Wafer Fab Expansion
current_status: EXPANSION IN PROGRESS; existing fab producing (Jan 2025 CHIPS non-binding memo up to $105M across 3 sites)
notes: Expansion of ADI's Beaverton fab (built 1978, ADI's largest wafer fab by volume): cleanroom to ~118,000 sq-ft, nearly doubling 180nm-and-above capacity, on top of ~950 existing Oregon employees. Jan 16, 2025 CHIPS non-binding memorandum for up to $105M covers Beaverton + Camas WA + Chelmsford MA (~500 jobs across all sites, not Beaverton-specific).

project: Johnson & Johnson Cell Therapy Manufacturing Facility (Lower Gwynedd, PA)
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION
notes: Cell therapy manufacturing for cancer/immune-mediated/neurological diseases on a 154-acre parcel in Lower Gwynedd Township, Montgomery County, PA. Capital stated as 'more than $1 billion' (recorded as the $1B floor). 500 figure is direct biomanufacturing jobs; the 4,000 construction jobs are excluded. Distinct from J&J's separate ~$2B Wilson, NC biologics site. Per WHYY, Pennsylvania is committing $41.5 million in tax credits and grants. Lead summary's claimed timeline (construction 2H 2026, production 2031) is NOT stated in either cited source, so it is not recorded on the row.

project: Highland Materials Polysilicon Plant (Project Rocks), Phipps Bend TN
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; engineering phase, on-site construction scheduled Q4 2026
notes: Solar-grade polysilicon plant ('Project Rocks') at former Phipps Bend nuclear site, Hawkins County (Surgoinsville), TN; classified Solar as a solar-supply-chain manufacturing facility (upstream polysilicon feedstock rather than cells/panels). Secured US$255.6M federal 48C tax credit April 2024. Initial capacity 16,000 t/yr rising to 20,000 t/yr within four years. ~140 acres of land secured. $1B total project cost from status_source. Construction start given as H2 2026 (pv-tech) / Q4 2026 (constructionreviewonline), consistent.

project: Slate Auto Warsaw EV Assembly Plant
current_status: PRE-PRODUCTION; factory nearing production, deliveries targeted Q4 2026, not yet producing
notes: Conversion of the former RR Donnelly & Sons printing plant (1.4M sq ft) near Warsaw, Kosciusko County, IN. Slate Auto based in Troy, MI. Status source (June 30, 2026) reports 180,000+ reservations and base price $24,950.

project: Stellantis Belvidere Assembly Plant
current_status: DELAYED; retooling underway (>$60M spent through July 2026); pilot production slipped to H1 2028, retail production H2 2029
notes: Belvidere idled Feb 2023 after Jeep Cherokee production ended. A late-2023 UAW contract agreement to reopen was reversed/delayed; Stellantis recommitted on Jan 24, 2025 to build an all-new mid-size pickup (targeted 2027). $335M DOE grant awarded July 2024 for EV conversion was put on hold. Investment $600M (announced fall 2025) later raised to more than $800M (Aug 2026); more than $60M spent through July 2026 on stamping, body, paint and general assembly. Plant to build the next-gen Jeep Cherokee on the new STLA One platform (minimum two vehicles, two shifts). Oct 2025 statement cited ~3,300 jobs and a 2027 launch; timeline has since slipped to pilot production H1 2028 / retail production H2 2029.

project: Gulf Coast Growth Ventures (Gregory, TX)
current_status: OPERATIONAL
notes: 50/50 ExxonMobil-SABIC petrochemical complex: 1.8 million t/yr ethane steam cracker, two polyethylene units and a monoethylene glycol unit near Gregory, San Patricio County, TX. Construction began Q3 2019 (~6,000 construction jobs). FAQ states project startup was completed in Q4 2021; BIC reports operations began Jan 20, 2022 with a community startup celebration on Mar 23, 2022.

project: ExxonMobil Baytown Low-Carbon Hydrogen Facility
current_status: PAUSED
notes: Blue-hydrogen facility at ExxonMobil's Baytown, TX complex: ~1 billion cubic feet/day of low-carbon hydrogen with >98% CO2 capture (~7 Mt/yr) plus low-carbon ammonia. FEED (front-end engineering and design) awarded to Technip Energies on 2023-01-30. Final investment decision targeted 2024, later updated to 2025, and startup later updated to 2029, per the release footnote. Cancelled/paused as reported Nov 2025 after failing to secure offtake customers and the spring-2025 withdrawal of a ~$332M DOE grant.

project: NXTClean Fuels Renewable Fuels Facility (Port Westward, Clatskanie)
current_status: PRE-CONSTRUCTION; not yet under construction, awaiting final federal permit (US Army Corps draft EIS in public comment through Apr 20, 2026; Corps decision expected summer 2026); operations targeted late 2028-2029
notes: Greenfield renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel refinery at Port Westward, Columbia County, OR; up to 50,000 barrels/day. $1.1B is the initial Aug 2018 announcement figure (proposed as Waterside Energy / NEXT Energy Group); the project was later cited at >$1B on the Sep 2019 port lease, ~$2B c. 2021 and ~$2.5B by 2025 - re-announcements per rule 4, not summed here. ~240 permanent jobs and 2,000 construction jobs per both sources. Oregon state permitting: removal-fill and air permits 2022, local land use permits 2024, DEQ 401 water permit approved Jan 7, 2025; final hurdle is the US Army Corps of Engineers federal permit. Formerly NEXT Renewable Fuels.
